headline: AI cloud companies Sharon AI and Lambda each announced on 1 Oct 2026 new loans, worth $356 million and $1 billion, that are secured against the AI chips they are buying.
score_reason: Lowered from 4: both announcements are dated 1 Oct 2026, before the 2 Oct window, and the terms are the companies' own statements.
importance_line: It affects lenders, AI cloud companies and their customers, and shows AI chips being used as collateral for loans, but all terms and customer figures come from the companies' own announcements.
summary: Company press releases show that Sharon AI, an Australian AI cloud provider, said it took a $356 million loan at a fixed 9.95% rate, and Lambda, a US AI cloud company, said it closed a $1 billion loan at 6.78%, both secured against the GPUs (the specialized chips that run AI) they are buying and against customer contracts. The 1 Oct 2026 announcements show how AI chip purchases are being paid for with loans tied to customer contracts, and the terms and the demand behind them are the companies' own statements.
notes: Original outlet Data Center Dynamics (HTTP 403, not opened); entry written from the two company releases, credited to their wire services. The link is Sharon AI's PR Newswire release; Lambda's Business Wire release was read at https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/lambda-closes-1-billion-senior-221700154.html.
